name: Honeywell Aerospace
description: Honeywell Aerospace was spun off from Honeywell on 2026-06-29 (one Aerospace share for every two Honeywell shares) and makes cockpit avionics and navigation systems, auxiliary power units and turbine engines, and aircraft control systems (air, thermal, motion, lighting). Its systems sit on about 90 percent of in-service aircraft and on more than 250 in-production platforms, so a large installed base keeps generating aftermarket spares, repairs and upgrades. In 2025 about 44 percent of net sales were commercial aftermarket, 15 percent commercial original equipment and 41 percent defense and space. It carries heavy new debt: $16.0B of notes issued 2026-03-16, $15.1B of net proceeds of which went to Honeywell in the separation.

businessLines.name: Electronic Solutions
businessLines.how: Sold to airframe makers and defense primes when platforms are built, then to operators for spares, repairs and retrofits over decades; defense customers buy through multi-year programmes.
businessLines.description: Avionics, navigation, cockpit and electronic systems for commercial, business-aviation and defense and space platforms.

operatingProfit.note: Segment profit (equals segment adjusted EBIT); FY2024 $1,912M (32 percent). Q2 2026 $459M vs $475M. Share of the three segments' $4,202M before $117M corporate cost (computed).

businessLines.name: Engines & Power Systems
businessLines.how: Engine and APU sales to aircraft makers, followed by long-tail aftermarket parts and repair for units in service; sales fell $312M in 2025 because of a Flexjet litigation settlement charge.
businessLines.description: Auxiliary power units (APUs), electrical power systems, turbine engines and related aftermarket; APUs have 95,000-plus deliveries and about 47,000 units in service.

revenue.note: After a $312M reduction for the Flexjet-related litigation settlement; FY2024 $4,731M. Q2 2026 $1,406M vs $1,390M.

businessLines.name: Control Systems
businessLines.how: Components sold to OEMs at build and to operators as replacement and repaired parts; Q1 2026 sales fell on lower commercial original equipment volumes.
businessLines.description: Air, thermal, motion, lighting and engine control systems for aircraft performance and cabin operations.

operatingProfit.note: Segment profit; FY2024 $1,226M (26 percent). Q2 2026 $389M vs $361M. Share of $4,202M (computed).
